page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8ae.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance engineered for workloads demanding higher memory-to-vCPU ratios. Operating on the KVM hypervisor with x86_64 architecture, the machine features an AMD EPYC 9T34 processor running at 3.4 GHz. The configuration allocates 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical execution cores via simultaneous multithreading. Cache resources include 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. The processor exposes advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16), VAES, and SHA-NI.

Memory density is the central structural attribute of the configuration, offering 32 GB of system memory at an exact allocation of 8 GB per vCPU. The instance provisions a 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. It contains zero local storage, requiring persistent state to be maintained on network-attached storage, and does not include GPU acceleration hardware.

Synthetic benchmark results highlight distinct performance tiers. Single-core compute capability is prominent, with stress-ng single-threaded results reaching the top tier and Geekbench single-core and text processing scores demonstrating strong per-clock efficiency. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics, including clang compilation, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and database operations, register in lower categories due to the physical constraint of 2 cores. From a resource perspective, the instance provides high qualitative efficiency for single-thread critical operations requiring large memory headroom, though it trades off high-throughput multi-core scaling.

Given its high memory-to-core allocation and strong single-thread execution, Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8ae.xlarge is suitable for in-memory caching systems, intermediate data processing layers, memory-sensitive analytics engines, and enterprise backend services that do not require dense parallel thread scaling or local NVMe storage.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8ae.xlarge is a memory-optimized KVM instance built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9T34 processor running at 3.4 GHz. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores and provides 32 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU ratio alongside a 4 Gbps baseline network link. The server includes no bundled local storage and no GPU hardware, relying on network-attached storage for disk operations. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier single-core CPU throughput and strong text processing, supported by modern instruction sets such as AVX-512 and VAES. However, multi-threaded tasks, database operations, and web throughput show lower benchmark scores, reflecting the two-core physical boundary. The instance is well suited for memory-intensive applications, in-memory caching platforms, and data processing services requiring strong single-thread compute alongside ample memory margins.
